title: Lalaport Transportation Hub: Bus Bays, Lockers, Lounge
metaDescription: Find the Lalaport Transportation Hub inside LaLaport BBCC: the way in from Hang Tuah station, check in, lockers, lounge and every bus that leaves from here.

contentBlocks.content: The Lalaport Transportation Hub is the bus terminal inside the LaLaport BBCC mall in Bukit Bintang. It is on Level LG1 of the East Atrium, at No. 2 Jalan Hang Tuah, and it is open 24 hours. Coaches leave here for Singapore, Johor, Melaka, Seremban, Hat Yai and both KL airports. The hub is linked to Hang Tuah station on the LRT and Monorail, and it is run by ttklia.com (The Straits Times).
This guide shows you how to find the hub inside the mall, what to do when you leave from it, what is there while you wait, and where the buses go.
Key Takeaways
Where is the Lalaport Transportation Hub? On Level LG1, East Atrium, of LaLaport Bukit Bintang City Centre (BBCC), No. 2 Jalan Hang Tuah, Kuala Lumpur.
Is it open at night? Yes, 24 hours. The mall's shops and restaurants keep normal mall hours, so late at night the hub is quiet.
Can I leave my bags there? Yes. There are 36 lockers near the bus bays, from RM20 to RM55 for 24 hours depending on size.
How do I get there by train? Take the LRT or Monorail to Hang Tuah station and walk across the covered link into the mall, then go down to LG1.
Where do buses go from Lalaport? Singapore, Johor, Melaka, Seremban, Hat Yai, KLIA2 and KLIA Terminal 1. You can book them on ttklia.com.
Finding the hub inside LaLaport BBCC

LaLaport BBCC has three atriums: West, Main and East. The hub is on the lower ground floor of the East Atrium. The train link comes into the opposite end of the mall, so give yourself a few extra minutes the first time.
From Hang Tuah LRT or Monorail station

Hang Tuah station is about a three minute walk from the mall along a covered walkway (LaLaport BBCC). The link brings you into Level 1 of the West Atrium. From there, go down to Level LG and walk through to the East Atrium. A quicker way with luggage: walk straight until you reach the max fashion store and take the lift just before it down to LG. Turn left out of the lift, walk past the food shops, and the hub signs are on your left (BusOnlineTicket).
From the MRT

On the MRT Kajang Line, get off at Merdeka MRT, take Exit B, and follow the signs towards Hang Tuah and BBCC (BusOnlineTicket). It is a longer walk than from Hang Tuah, so take Grab if you have heavy bags.
By Grab or taxi

Sources differ on the closest drop off. The mall names LaLaport Drop Off 2, the Jalan Hang Tuah entrance, as the closest e-hailing point to the hub (LaLaport BBCC). BusOnlineTicket names the Pudu Entrance on Level G, with a lift and escalator down to LG (BusOnlineTicket). Set either one in the app, then follow the signs for the Transportation Hub once you are inside.
Leaving from the hub
Buy your ticket before you arrive if you can. The hub has staffed ticket counters and self service kiosks, but a ticket on your phone saves a queue. Then:

• Check your boarding details. Your booking names the operator, the time and the pickup point. Bays vary by operator.
  • Check in and wait in the lounge. There is seating by the ticket counter and the cafeteria. Closer to departure, check in and go through to the waiting lounge.
  • Watch the screens. Departure screens like the ones at an airport show each coach and its status.
  • Board at your bay. Show your booking to the operator's staff at the gate.
Going to Singapore? Arrive early the first time, and have your passport and SG Arrival Card ready. Our KL to Singapore bus guide covers the border.
What is at the hub
Before the hub, many Singapore coaches stopped by the roadside at Berjaya Times Square. The hub has 11 bus bays and around 30 operators (LaLaport BBCC). Here is what you can use while you wait:

• Luggage lockers. 36 lockers near the bays, RM20 to RM55 for 24 hours by size. You can open yours as many times as you like within the 24 hours at no extra cost (The Straits Times).
  • Waiting lounge. Air conditioned, with power sockets for your phone or laptop.
  • Wi-Fi. Free inside the hub.
  • Cash. ATMs and money changers on the same floor, handy for ringgit or Singapore dollars.
  • Food. A CU convenience store for drinks and hot food, and ramen, Japanese curry and Korean barbecue restaurants in the mall.
  • Toilets and prayer rooms. Toilets in the hub, and separate surau for men and women on Level LG.
  • Access. Facilities for older travellers and wheelchair users, and 24 hour security monitoring.
  • Your SIM. If you booked a Teeko travel SIM, you can collect it at the tour centre at Lalaport BBCC. The exact counter details come with your booking.
Remember that the hub never closes but the mall does. If your coach leaves at 2 AM, eat before the restaurants shut and keep snacks in your bag. The supper guide lists late night food nearby.
Where buses go from Lalaport
These are the routes ttklia.com sells from the Lalaport hub. Pick your destination, then choose a date, time and operator on the booking page.

Shuttle vans to KLIA Terminal 1 and KLIA2 also leave from the hub. If you are flying out, our Bukit Bintang to KLIA2 guide compares the bus, the train and a taxi.

contentBlocks.content: Arriving at Lalaport

When your coach pulls in, you step off indoors on LG1. Store your bags in a locker if your hotel room is not ready, get cash, and head up to the train. Coming from Singapore? Our Singapore to KL bus guide covers the border, the MDAC and what to check on your ticket.
Getting around from the hub

Hang Tuah station is on the Ampang and Sri Petaling LRT lines and the KL Monorail. The Monorail runs to Bukit Bintang in two stops and to KL Sentral at the end of the line. For short hops, the BOLEH BOLEH Ride on demand van covers Pudu, Bukit Bintang and Imbi for RM4 per adult ride, booked in the mobi app, with up to RM2 more at peak times (LaLaport BBCC).
Staying a few days? See our guide to things to do in Bukit Bintang, with the train or walk to each place.
Frequently Asked Questions
Where is the Lalaport Transportation Hub?

The Lalaport Transportation Hub is on Level LG1, East Atrium, of the LaLaport BBCC mall at No. 2 Jalan Hang Tuah, Bukit Bintang. It is linked to Hang Tuah LRT and Monorail station by a covered walkway.
Is the Lalaport Transportation Hub open 24 hours?
Yes. The Lalaport Transportation Hub is open 24 hours, so night coaches arrive and leave there. The mall's shops and restaurants keep normal hours, so plan food around that.
Are there luggage lockers at Lalaport?
Yes. The Lalaport hub has 36 luggage lockers near the bus bays, from RM20 to RM55 for 24 hours depending on size. You can open yours as often as you need within the 24 hours.
Where does Grab drop off for the Lalaport bus terminal?

The mall names LaLaport Drop Off 2, the Jalan Hang Tuah entrance, as the closest e-hailing point to the bus terminal. BusOnlineTicket suggests the Pudu Entrance. From either, follow the signs down to LG1, East Atrium.
Can I take a bus from Lalaport to the airport?
Yes. Buses run from Lalaport to KLIA2 and to KLIA Terminal 1, and you can book them on ttklia.com. Check which terminal your flight uses first.
Conclusion

The Lalaport Transportation Hub puts an indoor, 24 hour bus terminal on the train line in Bukit Bintang. Come in from Hang Tuah station, head for LG1 in the East Atrium, and leave your bags in a locker if you have time to kill. When you are ready to go, book your bus from Lalaport on ttklia.com.
